inspection_summary: Inspected all 1,447 Python splitlines() logical lines of the hash-bound normalized article. The usable mathematical text comprises the introduction; the curve-decoupling theorem and bootstrap proof; the specialized A6 mean-value theorem and bilinear-to-linear proof; the Bombieri-Iwaniec application separating first and second spacing; parameter optimization for exponential sums; the zeta critical-line transfer; and the exponent-pair extension. Formula extraction is typographically fragmented in places but no mathematical passage selected below is unrecoverable: claims were bounded to what the checked prose and numbered displays jointly support. The source contains no prior v1 units to carry or repair.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter, abstract, introduction, and method map
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the sharp A6 target, the 13/84 zeta consequence, and the first-spacing/second-spacing decomposition of the Bombieri-Iwaniec method.

sections_inspected.label: 1 A decoupling inequality for curves
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Formulates the even-dimensional multilinear decoupling theorem, relates it to known endpoints, derives transversality, and proves it by quadratic factorization and scale iteration.

sections_inspected.label: 2 A mean value theorem
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Specializes to the four-coordinate curve, repairs domain shape and bilinear/linear gaps, proves the sharp twelfth moment, and records its anisotropic A6 corollary.

sections_inspected.label: 3 Applications to exponential sums
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Inserts the new first-spacing bound into a double-large-sieve framework, combines it with imported second-spacing estimates, and optimizes scales to prove Theorem 4.

sections_inspected.label: 4 Bounding the zeta-function on the critical line
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Covers the remaining short-sum ranges with known estimates, applies the approximate functional equation, and interprets the resulting saving.

sections_inspected.label: 5 Further comments
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Promotes the estimate to an exponent pair by scale renormalization, the B-process, and extension from subinterval phases.

sections_inspected.label: References
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliographic support only; no independent semantic unit selected.

accepted_units.title: Sharp sixth moment as the decoupling target
accepted_units.why_material: The introduction identifies the essentially sharp A6 mean-value estimate as the paper's objective and states that it will be obtained from a curve-decoupling theorem, clarifying both the target quantity and the intended analytical bridge.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the displayed A6 expression, the comparison with the earlier A5 input, and the forward references to Theorems 1 and 2.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the extracted display (0.1), whose exponents are recoverable from the formula and surrounding prose.

accepted_units.title: Bombieri-Iwaniec first- and second-spacing architecture
accepted_units.why_material: The source decomposes the zeta-function route into short cubic-phase sums, a first-spacing distribution of (h,h^2,h^(3/2),h^(1/2)), a second-spacing distribution of interval-dependent phase vectors, and a double-large-sieve interface. It explicitly limits the paper's new input to the first spacing problem.
accepted_units.context_note: The passage also explains why an r-fold convolution turns the first spacing distribution into the mean value studied later and states that external second-spacing estimates remain necessary.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The conceptual split is prose-grounded; the four-coordinate vectors and short-sum phase require formulas (0.2)-(0.4).

accepted_units.title: Multilinear decoupling for even-dimensional nondegenerate curves
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 1 gives the central scale-sensitive decoupling inequality for separated arcs of an even-dimensional curve under a Wronskian nondegeneracy condition, reducing an L^(3d) multilinear quantity to L^6 pieces on N^(-1/2) parameter intervals.
accepted_units.context_note: The span includes the averaged norm convention, the exact hypotheses, and the suppressed weighted-norm technicality.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent: the exponents, interval scale, and norm normalization are essential; the extraction is fragmented typographically but recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Two gaps from bilinear decoupling to the A6 mean value
accepted_units.why_material: The source isolates two distinct obstacles between Theorem 1 and Theorem 2: replacing ball averages by a smaller anisotropic periodic region, and converting a bilinear estimate into a linear one. This is a reusable decomposition of the proof burden.
accepted_units.context_note: The specialized curve and target region are stated before the two remedies are assigned to the two halves of Section 2.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Uses the displayed anisotropic box and specialized curve coordinates; the two-obstacle analysis is explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Planar L6 decoupling as the operative lower-dimensional input
accepted_units.why_material: The remarks identify planar nonzero-curvature L6 decoupling, including its discrete coefficient form, as the main analytical input for the higher-dimensional theorem.
accepted_units.context_note: The span also records translation invariance of the main estimate, which is used when localizing to cubes.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires formulas (1.5) and its discrete version for the precise norm and scale; prose makes the input role clear.

accepted_units.title: Positioning the new inequality between multilinear endpoints
accepted_units.why_material: The Fourier-support reformulation relates the theorem to known d-linear and (d-1)-linear decouplings, and shows that the latter exponent pair is obtained by interpolation between the elementary Parseval endpoint and the new (3d,6) endpoint.
accepted_units.context_note: The discussion also explains why even dimension is built into the result and why d=4 is the application-relevant case.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strongly formula-dependent because the endpoint pairs and Fourier-tube geometry carry the comparison; the prose supplies the interpolation claim.

accepted_units.title: Preliminary interpolation bound and paired-tangent transversality
accepted_units.why_material: An L^d estimate derived by randomization and a trivial L-infinity bound are interpolated via wave packets to a preliminary L^(3d)-L6 inequality. The Wronskian condition is then converted into the wedge-product transversality of paired first and second derivatives needed for factorization.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the local K-cube version and explains that its coarse K^(1/3) loss is only a bootstrap seed.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on equations (1.12)-(1.17), especially the interval scale and wedge determinant; extracted prose preserves the logical transitions.

accepted_units.title: Bootstrap by quadratic normal forms and product factorization
accepted_units.why_material: The proof partitions the large ball into K-cubes, Taylor-expands each separated arc to quadratic order, uses transversality to turn the ambient integral into a product of planar factors, applies planar decoupling after rescaling, and obtains b(N) bounded by b(N^(2/3)) up to N^epsilon.
accepted_units.context_note: The scale restriction N=o(K^(3/2)) and the harmless-multiplier treatment of the Taylor remainder are included because they justify the iteration.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent: the quadratic phase, change of variables, scale relation, and recurrence are essential, though their role is explicitly narrated.

accepted_units.title: Specializing decoupling to d=4 and an anisotropic intermediate box
accepted_units.why_material: Section 2 specializes the curve, imposes the derivative condition needed by the application, enlarges the averaging domain to an anisotropic box, partitions it into N-cubes, and transfers Theorem 1 to a bilinear discrete estimate prepared for a second decoupling.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the first half of the domain-shape repair announced in lines 204-206.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires formulas (2.1)-(2.4), the coordinate choices, and box dimensions; several display lines are fragmented but reconstructible.

accepted_units.title: Taylor-periodicity normal form for separated short intervals
accepted_units.why_material: For two separated length-N^(1/2) intervals, Taylor expansion plus periodic changes of variables converts the coupled phases into independent planar quadratic phases. Planar decoupling then refines the interval scale to N^(1/4), with an explanation of why a residual term can be absorbed.
accepted_units.context_note: The separation and third-derivative hypotheses are used to make the x2,x3 change of variables nondegenerate.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The mechanism depends on expansions (2.5), normal forms (2.6), factorization (2.7), and estimate (2.8); prose checks the discarded-term change of variables.

accepted_units.title: Aggregation over translated boxes and final bilinear estimate
accepted_units.why_material: The argument tiles the larger Huxley box by translated intermediate boxes, carries the phase translation into coefficients, and repeats the periodic/Taylor normalization at the N^(1/4) scale. Planar L6 control then yields the decisive bilinear L12 estimate on the full anisotropic domain.
accepted_units.context_note: The exact derivative determinant condition for the specialized curve is recorded at the end of the span.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the anisotropic regions and formulas (2.9)-(2.11); the factorization steps remain intelligible despite display fragmentation.

accepted_units.title: Essentially sharp A6 mean value theorem
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 2 states the twelfth-moment bound N^(6+epsilon) for the four-coordinate exponential sum that supplies the optimal first-spacing input.
accepted_units.context_note: The theorem is stated immediately after deriving the applicable bilinear curve estimate.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Entirely tied to display (2.12); the four phase coordinates and twelfth power define the result.

accepted_units.title: Encoding moment solutions by a normalized nondegenerate curve
accepted_units.why_material: The proof interprets a localized bilinear moment as a solution count, expands the fractional powers around a base point, uses the first two exact moment equations to cancel low-order terms, and packages the remaining constraints into a curve satisfying the earlier derivative condition. The bilinear estimate then bounds the localized count.
accepted_units.context_note: The span retains the system of equations, Taylor normalizations, and the resulting bound N^(4+epsilon)M^2.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Highly formula-dependent; the prose and numbered expansions (2.14)-(2.23) make the cancellations and rescaling recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Bilinear-to-linear conversion by recursive interval decomposition
accepted_units.why_material: A Bourgain-Guth style broad/narrow decomposition recursively partitions the summation interval, controls separated pairs with the localized bilinear estimate, and derives a contraction recurrence for the linear twelfth moment.
accepted_units.context_note: The decreasing-rearrangement dichotomy underlying the pointwise split and the summability of scale contributions are both included.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires formulas (2.24)-(2.27) for coefficients and contraction; the proof architecture is also stated in prose.

accepted_units.title: Anisotropically rescaled first-spacing estimate
accepted_units.why_material: Corollary 3 converts Theorem 2 into Huxley's A6(N,delta,Delta) notation and supplies the delta*Delta*N^(9+epsilon) bound later inserted directly into the large sieve.
accepted_units.context_note: The source notes that the major-arc contribution makes the estimate essentially best possible.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula (2.28) is essential because the two anisotropic scale parameters define the later identification.

accepted_units.title: Reduction of smooth exponential sums to interval phase vectors
accepted_units.why_material: The application fixes derivative nondegeneracy, introduces the intermediate scales N and R, and cites the established Bombieri-Iwaniec reduction that bounds the original sum using short sums indexed by minor-arc intervals and four-dimensional phase vectors.
accepted_units.context_note: The source explicitly declines to reproduce the second-spacing map and identifies it with prior work, so this unit records a dependency rather than an internally proved step.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Uses formulas (3.1)-(3.4) and the coordinate ranges; the construction of x(I) is intentionally external.

accepted_units.title: Holder reduction to a sixfold first-spacing distribution
accepted_units.why_material: An interval-count estimate, the preliminary sum bound, and sixth-power Holder produce a dichotomy: either a direct bound holds or the problem reduces to a bilinear sum coupling interval phase vectors with a sixfold convolution of the first-spacing curve.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the admissible Q range and the definition of the six-coordinate aggregate y(h).
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on equations (3.5)-(3.7) and the displayed y(h) vector.

accepted_units.title: Double large sieve separates the two spacing problems
accepted_units.why_material: The double large sieve bounds the coupled phase sum by the geometric mean of a first-spacing count A and a second-spacing count B1, times coordinate-volume factors, cleanly isolating what the new mean-value theorem can control from what must be imported.
accepted_units.context_note: The source explains that two coordinates of the approximate first-spacing conditions are actually integer equalities.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires formulas (3.8)-(3.9) and the definitions of A and B1; the conceptual separation is explicit.

accepted_units.title: First-spacing count identified with A6
accepted_units.why_material: Fourier localization turns the first-spacing count A into a scaled A6 integral with delta=Q^2/(H^2R^2), after which Corollary 3 yields A bounded by delta^2 H^(10+epsilon). This is the direct causal interface from decoupling to the large sieve.
accepted_units.context_note: The admissibility check 1/H <= H*delta <= Q/N <= 1 is included before applying the corollary.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent: the Fourier integral, rescaling, and delta identification are the substance of the unit.

accepted_units.title: Combining first and baseline second spacing bounds
accepted_units.why_material: An imported second-spacing estimate for B1 is combined with the new A bound and the large-sieve reduction; choosing N=M*T^(-2/7) yields the exponential-sum estimate with exponent 13/84 over its initial M range.
accepted_units.context_note: The provenance of the B1 estimate is explicit and the scale conditions R<=N<=R^2 are checked for the stated range.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on formulas (3.11)-(3.13) and the parameter relation (3.3); the second-spacing ingredient is not proved here.

accepted_units.title: Resonance-curve tightening of the second-spacing window
accepted_units.why_material: The source introduces a tunable factor V that narrows one coordinate window in the second-spacing count while enlarging the adjacent volume factor, allowing Huxley's resonance-curve estimate for BV to replace the baseline B1 bound.
accepted_units.context_note: This refinement is used specifically to extend the M range; its imported status and alternative choices of V are retained.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires formulas (3.14)-(3.15), the modified spacing window, and the Delta parameters.

accepted_units.title: Optimizing the resonance bound across scale regimes
accepted_units.why_material: Combining the refined large-sieve and second-spacing bounds produces a minimum of competing terms. Optimizing N, then switching to N comparable to R^2 when the first optimizer violates a scale constraint, yields piecewise bounds that extend the desired estimate down to M>=T^(17/42).
accepted_units.context_note: The span preserves the regime boundaries and explicitly explains the constraint-driven switch of scale.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent: equations (3.16)-(3.18) and the N,R relations determine the optimization.

accepted_units.title: Uniform exponential-sum estimate in the large-alpha range
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 4 packages the preceding parameter analysis into the estimate |S| bounded by M^(1/2)T^(13/84+epsilon) for log M/log T between 17/42 and 1/2.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the internal exponential-sum output later combined with complementary known estimates.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The short theorem is defined by display (3.19), including its alpha range.

accepted_units.title: Covering complementary scales and transferring to zeta
accepted_units.why_material: Two external exponential-sum bounds cover the alpha range below Theorem 4, with an overlap calculation ensuring full coverage. For the logarithmic phase relevant to zeta, the approximate functional equation, partial summation, and dyadic dissection then transfer the uniform short-sum estimate to the critical-line bound.
accepted_units.context_note: The source flags additional hypotheses on the general phase and explains why log x satisfies them; the final transfer is summarized rather than reproved.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Uses inequalities (4.1)-(4.3), interval arithmetic for alpha, and the approximate-functional-equation display.

accepted_units.title: Moment order and the doubling of the critical-line saving
accepted_units.why_material: The remark compares essentially optimal A4, A5, and A6 inputs and interprets the 13/84 exponent as exactly doubling the original Bombieri-Iwaniec saving over 1/6.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a source-authored interpretation of how improved first-spacing moments translate into zeta exponents, with the historical caveat about difficult alpha cases.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the displayed rational-exponent identities; the comparative claim is stated in prose.

accepted_units.title: From the paper's estimate to an exponent pair
accepted_units.why_material: The source reformulates the result as the exponent pair (13/84,55/84), handles scales with M above the square root by renormalizing T or applying the B-process after Poisson summation, and notes the fixed-point relation of the relevant pair under B.
accepted_units.context_note: Extreme large-M cases are separately secured by the classical (1/2,1/2) pair.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires the exponent-pair formulas and scale substitutions; the Poisson/B-process details are cited rather than reproduced.

accepted_units.title: Extending partial-interval phases to use exponent-pair theory
accepted_units.why_material: To remove the full-interval assumption, the source constructs a smooth extension of the phase from [a,b] to [M/2,M] using a monomial derivative model plus a correcting polynomial, argues that derivative conditions persist, and then invokes an interval-restriction lemma at logarithmic cost.
accepted_units.context_note: This resolves the second explicit obstacle in promoting the estimate to a general exponent-pair statement.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The construction uses the displayed integral-polynomial extension and derivative-condition prose; the cited restriction lemma supplies the final localization.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Multiscale factorization engine
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Across both the abstract curve theorem and its arithmetic specialization, the recurring mechanism is to localize in scale, Taylor-normalize separated pieces, use transversality and periodicity to factor the phase into lower-dimensional pieces, decouple those pieces, and close a larger-scale statement by iteration or broad/narrow decomposition.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The synthesis is conditional on the stated Wronskian and derivative nondegeneracy, even dimension for Theorem 1, and the specialized arithmetic curve; it does not assert the mechanism for arbitrary curves or odd dimensions.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Causal chain from first-spacing decoupling to the zeta exponent
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The sharp A6 estimate controls exactly the first-spacing count A in the double large sieve; when paired with separately sourced second-spacing bounds and optimized intermediate scales, it improves smooth exponential sums, and complementary range estimates plus the approximate functional equation transfer that improvement to the critical line.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source does not derive the second-spacing estimates, the complementary Huxley/exponent-pair bounds, or the approximate functional equation; the final implication is therefore a composite result rather than decoupling alone.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Intermediate scale choice as an interface between analytic modules
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Scale parameters are not bookkeeping: K enables contraction in decoupling and bilinear-to-linear bootstraps, while N and V balance first-spacing strength, second-spacing resolution, and admissibility constraints in the exponential-sum application.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The specific exponents and optimizers belong to this proof's inequalities and should not be generalized without re-deriving the competing terms.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: From a bounded-range estimate to an exponent-pair statement
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A strong estimate on one natural scale range becomes a reusable exponent-pair result only after complementary estimates cover missing ranges, the B-process handles dual large scales, and a controlled phase extension removes the full-interval assumption.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Several steps are cited from established exponent-pair theory and the construction assumes its derivative and monomial-approximation hypotheses.
